questions.question: Psychology is best defined as the scientific study of:
questions.explanation: Behaviour (observable) and mental processes (thoughts, feelings) are both studied.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The first psychological laboratory was established in 1879 by:
questions.explanation: Marks the beginning of scientific psychology.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Behaviourism emphasises:

options.B: Observable behaviour and the role of learning and environment

questions.explanation: Founded by John Watson; Skinner developed operant conditioning.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The humanistic approach to psychology is associated with:
questions.explanation: Emphasis on growth and self-actualisation.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In Freud's structural model of personality, the ‘ego’ operates on the:
questions.explanation: The id works on the pleasure principle; the superego on morality.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Attributing one's own unacceptable feelings to another person is called:
questions.explanation: Repression is pushing unwanted thoughts out of awareness.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In Pavlov's experiment the bell, after repeated pairing with food, became a:
questions.explanation: Salivation to the bell alone is the conditioned response.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Operant conditioning was studied mainly by:
questions.explanation: Behaviour is shaped by its consequences.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Taking away an unpleasant stimulus to increase a behaviour is:
questions.explanation: Punishment reduces the probability of a behaviour.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which reinforcement schedule produces behaviour most resistant to extinction?
questions.explanation: Gambling machines use variable-ratio reinforcement.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Bandura's Bobo doll experiment demonstrated:
questions.explanation: Children imitate models.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The correct sequence of memory stages in the Atkinson–Shiffrin model is:

options.A: Sensory memory, short-term memory, long-term memory

questions.explanation: Attention transfers information from sensory to short-term memory.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The capacity of short-term memory is about:
questions.explanation: Miller's magical number seven; chunking increases capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Without rehearsal, information in short-term memory lasts about:
questions.explanation: Rehearsal maintains it.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Forgetting because new learning interferes with the recall of earlier learning is called:
questions.explanation: Proactive: old learning interferes with new.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Riding a bicycle is stored in:
questions.explanation: Declarative memory includes episodic and semantic.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Inability to form new memories after an injury is called:
questions.explanation: Retrograde amnesia is loss of memories before the event.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In Piaget's theory, object permanence develops in the:
questions.explanation: Conservation develops in the concrete operational stage.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The correct sequence of Piaget's stages is:

options.B: Sensorimotor, preoperational, concrete operational, formal operational

questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: According to Erikson, the psychosocial crisis of adolescence is:
questions.explanation: Infancy: trust vs mistrust; toddler: autonomy vs shame.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Attachment theory was developed by:
questions.explanation: The ‘Strange Situation’ test classifies attachment styles.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Kohlberg's theory deals with the development of:
questions.explanation: Levels: pre-conventional, conventional, post-conventional.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: At the top of Maslow's hierarchy of needs is:
questions.explanation: Physiological needs form the base.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The James–Lange theory of emotion states that:

options.D: We feel emotion because we perceive our bodily responses

questions.explanation: The Cannon–Bard theory says they occur simultaneously.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Aggression resulting from frustration is described by the:
questions.explanation: Dollard and Miller (1939).
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The intelligence quotient is calculated as:

options.C: Mental age divided by chronological age multiplied by 100
options.D: Chronological age divided by mental age

questions.explanation: A person of average intelligence has an IQ of about 100.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The first practical intelligence test was developed by:
questions.explanation: Binet–Simon scale (1905) to identify children needing help.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The theory of multiple intelligences was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Includes linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal and intrapersonal intelligence.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the Big Five personality traits?
questions.explanation: The Big Five: OCEAN.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Eysenck's three dimensions of personality are:
questions.explanation: Measured by the EPQ.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Rorschach inkblot test is an example of a:
questions.explanation: TAT is another projective test.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cognitive dissonance theory was proposed by:
questions.explanation: People change attitudes to reduce the tension of inconsistent beliefs.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Asch's experiments demonstrated:
questions.explanation: Milgram studied obedience.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The bystander effect refers to the finding that:

options.A: People are less likely to help when others are present
options.B: Helping is unrelated to presence of others
options.D: People help more in a crowd

questions.explanation: Diffusion of responsibility.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The three stages of Selye's General Adaptation Syndrome are:
questions.explanation: Prolonged stress leads to exhaustion and illness.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Type A personality (competitive, time-urgent, hostile) is associated with an increased risk of:
questions.explanation: Hostility is the most toxic component.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Problem-focused coping involves:

options.A: Taking direct action to change the stressful situation

questions.explanation: Emotion-focused coping manages emotional response.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Social Readjustment Rating Scale (Holmes and Rahe) rates the highest stress for:
questions.explanation: Used to predict illness after life change units.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The consistency of a psychological test over time is called its:
questions.explanation: Validity is whether the test measures what it claims to measure.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A correlation between two variables shows that:

options.B: They vary together but does not prove causation

questions.explanation: Experiments are required to infer cause.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Weber's law states that:

options.C: The just-noticeable difference is a constant proportion of the original stimulus

questions.explanation: Used in psychophysics.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The trichromatic theory of colour vision proposes:

options.A: Three types of cones sensitive to red, green and blue
options.B: Colour is perceived in the brain only

questions.explanation: The opponent-process theory explains afterimages.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Sleepwalking and night terrors occur during:
questions.explanation: Nightmares occur in REM sleep.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology (chapter-level reference)
